Hayden turned to the group as Jared and Beck took their seats on each side. God, when they were in the same frame, they looked good enough to eat, and she had heard many women and men say the same thing over the years.
 
“I’ve called this meeting because I’ll be away for at least 2 months, or possibly longer, and want to make sure you understand that you will be unable to contact me at all during that time, so I will be assigning one person to stand in my place.” He nodded at Anna, his attorney. ‘That includes all decisions concerning anything involving Oakley Corp., both legal issues and financial.”
 
Hayden paused and looked around to note their reactions to the news. He continued, “I discussed this matter with Myla…”
 
“Oh, please,” Scott interrupted, “no disrespect intended, but don’t you think that role is more fit for someone with business intellect? Your wife probably can handle household problems well, but she’s definitely not qualified to handle the responsibilities you’ve outlined.”
 
Scott looked at the others in the room like he was challenging them as he continued. “With my degree in finance and my experience in running my own business, surely I am the most qualified person in this room.”
“Well, Scott,” Hayden said in a cool voice. “Myla actually declined my offer for her to run my operations in my absence. She is in the process of finalizing the sale of another business of hers. You have heard of My-Design, Inc., haven’t you?”
 
Myla watched with satisfaction as Scott’s jaw dropped in shock.
 
“That’s the business Myla started and built into the international business it is today with just an idea and her hard work. Myla is more than qualified for anything she chooses to do.” He finished coldly.
He turned back to the rest of the group. “Deciding who would be acting on my behalf was a ‘no-brainer’ for me. But, because my first option said no, effective the twenty-fifth of next month, all financial and corporate problems should be referred to, and decisions will be made by Beck Garner. Jared Lotto will be handling all finances related to the estate and other properties.”
 
Before anyone could say anything, Scott jumped up, his face red. “I don’t believe I am the only one who thinks this is the most ridiculous decision ever. You can’t seriously be giving all of that power to some glorified bodyguards?” he sneered, looking around the room, hoping to see that the others will agree with him. But they all looked at his outburst with disgust.
“No, seriously, what experience does either one have in dealing with major financial decisions or running a business, or anything else for that matter? They’re just hired muscle for Christ’s sake.”
 
Hayden’s body stiffened, and his eyes narrowed in anger as he watched Scott.
would
“Walker,” snarled Scott to the manager of the company. “You can’t tell me that you want a bodyguard coming into your office, telling you how to run the company.”
 
“Well, Scott,” Walker drawled coldly, “those mere bodyguards are also the owners of the thriving J&B Security firm, plus they handled things well when Hayden was hospitalized and know exactly what Hayden would do in any given situation concerning the corporation.”
 
Scott’s face got redder at his words.
 
“And,” Walker continued, “we’ve all seen Beck and Jared make several suggestions over the last few years that saved Oak Corps more than tens of thousands of dollars. I admit I would hire him in a minute as my vice president if I wasn’t sure he’d have my job within a month, or less.”
 
Everyone laughed as Beck made a slight bow to Walker.
 
Hayden grinned and said, “Walker, I can assure you your job is safe from Beck.” He turned to Scott, his smile disappearing. “You, I wanted to do this in private, but since you decided to be so open today, let me follow your lead…” He turned and nodded at Anna.
 
Anna smiled. “Mrs. Oakley noticed some inconsistencies in the accounts and called our attention to them. We investigated and discovered that you have been siphoning funds from the company. Care to explain?”
Scott looked wildly around the room. “This is a fucking setup! Everyone knows that these two bitches never liked me. Y’all can’t possibly believe them over me—’
 
“Enough!” Myla shouted as she shot up from her seat, glaring at Scott. “First, we have enough evidence against you, so I suggest you prepare your lawyers. Secondly, you have no right to question any decisions we make. If we wanted your opinion, we would have asked for it. Now, either sit down and shut up, or get out.”
 
Hayden’s chest expanded with pride as he watched his wife. Jared and Beck exchanged a smile before they turned their attention back to Scott.
 
Scott’s face was contorted in rage, spit spraying from his mouth as he screamed, “Ooh, I get it now. Hubby can’t get it up, so you’re fucking the bodyguards. Everyone has heard the rumors that the three of them used to share their women all the time, and it looks like they’re still sharing!”

BENEATH THE BRUISES
Myla stared at him, dumbfounded, for a few seconds. Then she sneered, “Where did you hear such a ridiculous rumor? First, you’re a crook, now a gossipmonger?” She laughed in his face, then continued. “You’re pathetic, and you will be hearing from our lawyers soon. You are done. Just get out of here.”
 “Get out of my way, bitch.” He roughly tried to force Myla to back up as he pushed by her, deliberately hitting her in the stomach with his elbow.
Myla gasped, then punched him back hard. Scott staggered back and tripped over his fallen chair. He lunged forward, trying to keep his balance, and fell full force on her, knocking her to the floor. Her head hit the marble floor hard, and the sound echoed through the room.
 Hayden’s bellow of rage filled the room.
 Jared vaulted the conference table and roughly grabbed Scott off her. Beck was already at Myla’s side, checking her over as Hayden rolled up beside him.
 Setting Scott on his feet, Jared plowed his fist into Scott’s midsection. The blow knocked Scott into the wall, and he slid down to the floor, vomiting all over himself and groaning as he held his stomach.
Myla moaned softly and tried to get up, but Beck gently held her down. “Take it easy, Myla. You hit your head pretty hard there.
Myla’s vision swam as she laughed weakly but didn’t try to get up again.
“Jared!” Beck yelled when he saw him preparing to hit Scott again. “Don’t waste your energy on that waste of space. It may take time before the ambulance gets here; we need to get her to the hospital. You know how tricky head wounds can be, and I’m not liking the dazed look in her eyes right now.”
Hayden looked coldly at Scott, then raised his eyes to the stunned gazes of those left standing at the conference table. “Meeting over! Someone get that asshole out of my sight. As far as I’m concerned, he can stink up his own car until a tow truck can move it out of here. Anna, I’ll call you tomorrow. I want legal steps taken to shut that filthy mouth of his.”
“Okay, boss. Am I correct in assuming you are also going to pull your financial portfolio from his firm?” Anna asked smugly.
 
“Immediately, thanks for reminding me.”
 “Hayden,” said Carter spoke up cautiously as Jared gently picked Myla up. “I don't think Scott meant to deliberately hurt Myla.”
“I don't know, Carter; to me it looked like he deliberately tried to knock Myla aside as roughly as he could, and he has a nasty reputation for physically abusing the women he’s been associated with in the past. I don’t think he’s changed.”
Carter nodded in understanding.
Hayden turned to Scott, moaning, shaking from. “All these years, I have ignored the derogatory words you use with women and your alcoholism, but you crossed the line when you dared to harm my wife. I will fucking ruin you.” He growled out. Then followed Jared as he carried Myla out, with Beck closely behind.
* * * * * * * *
Jared placed Myla in Beck's arms, got into the SUV, and then Beck gently placed her back in his arms. She curled instinctively into his lap as he cradled her like she was made of glass.
Hayden wheeled himself in and locked into position, his eyes never leaving her face. Beck slid into the front passenger seat beside the driver, giving a clipped order to move.
 The car sped off.
 The air inside was tight with worry.
Jared glanced down at her, gently brushing hair from her damp forehead. Her eyes were unfocused, her breathing was shallow, and she kept mumbling random things under her breath.
She blinked slowly, her lips parting like she was about to speak. But her words were slurred. “Don’t... take...”
“Myla, don't what?” He asked as he leaned down to hear better.
"Don't... to Crest hospi..." she mumbled, barely above a whisper.
 
“It’s the closest, honey,” Jared said softly, finally understanding her.
 Her brow creased. She whined, a soft, childlike sound. “No... no, not there... too many bad memories... don’t want to go...”
Jared looked up, eyes flicking to the rearview mirror where Beck's worried eyes met his. It was the same place Hayden had been rushed to after the accident.
Then she started thrashing slightly, still mumbling, No... no, under her breath.
“It’s okay,” Hayden said quietly, his voice low and warm. “We won’t go there, baby. We’ll go somewhere else.”
“Okay,” she breathed out. Then she started humming a broken melody under her breath.
Hayden let out a worried sigh. "She is getting more loopy." He looked at the driver. "Steve to St Veronica, I have already texted the MD that we're coming. Speed up." He said sharply as he reached over and caressed her hair.
She leaned into the touch, then suddenly turned her head toward him, startling him, and Jared quickly adjusted to support her head better.
“You’re touching me,” she whispered like she was amazed. Then she gave him a sleepy smile. “It’s been so long since you touched and looked at me like that...”
She blinked slowly, her eyes glassy. “I thought you didn’t love me anymore.”
Hayden’s breath caught. The words hit like a knife in his gut. He swallowed hard, opened his mouth to speak—
But her eyes rolled back, and she slumped deeper into Jared’s chest.
“Myla!” Jared panicked, tapping her cheek repeatedly. "Hey... hey... come on, sweetheart, open your eyes—”
"I felt a bump on her head; make sure she doesn't fall asleep,” Hayden said, panicked.
 
A beat later, her eyes fluttered open.
She blinked slowly, dazed. Jared let out a heavy breath of relief.
“Just try to stay awake, baby,” he murmured, nuzzling her hair. “We’re almost there.”
She made a soft sound and curled tighter into him.
When they pulled up to the clinic, two nurses were already waiting with a gurney. Jared placed her on it, and they all watched grimly as she was wheeled away.
Hayden sat still, his chair by the tall windows, staring at the sterile white floor. Beck leaned against the wall while Jared paced.
Her words echoed again and again in Hayden's head: “I thought you didn’t love me anymore.”
He closed his eyes as his chest clenched painfully.
After the accident, everything had changed. The months of pain, different experts and specialists, long surgeries, and long, sleepless nights in a hospital bed, unable to move. He had thought he knew devastation when the doctor had told him he would never walk again. But the worst came when he found out he was impotent.
Something inside him had cracked open and bled dry that day. The crash didn't just physically break him; it also stripped him of what made him a man.
He had always loved Myla with his whole being; their one year of dating and two years of marriage had been heaven. Their sex life had been raw, wild, and consuming. He used to take her up against walls, bend her over the kitchen counter, and wake her up with his mouth between her thighs.
And suddenly… He couldn't stand or walk... couldn't even get hard.
So what did he have left to offer her.
He became bitter... angry. Hated himself for needing help to do basic things; her comfort and care felt like pity. He felt like he was watching her try to love a ghost.
He started pulling away, locked in his head. Even Jared and Beck had confronted him more than once, telling him to stop pushing her away.
But he didn’t know how to face her without feeling like a useless failure of a man.
He thought he was sparing her from the burden that he had become.
Now he saw the truth. All that time, she had been hurting, too. And his mercy had made her believe he didn’t love her anymore.
He rubbed a hand over his mouth, his throat aching as he looked out the window.
But there was one thing none of them knew, one thing he had never told a soul.
He remembered one thing too clearly from the hit and run. Seconds before the masked-up driver hit him, he had winked and saluted Hayden.
The crash was no accident. It had been an assassination attempt.
And with the latest evidence he got recently, it seems like they were not done yet.

THREE MUSKETEERS & A PUSH-MOBILE
“So... you three were in the habit of sharing your women.” Myla blurted out before she could stop herself. “And what am I? Chopped liver?”

Those were the first words she said to them immediately after they stepped into her room this morning. The doctor had kept her for observation, worried about her slurred speech and the large bump on her head. Myla hadn't seen them since the nurses chased them away late last night after visiting hours.

Myla started laughing so hard she could barely catch her breath at the pure shock plastered across their faces. “Oh my God, you should see your faces,” she managed through gasps of laughter. “I’m so glad the painkillers have finally kicked in, or I’d be in agony right now. Whew! Your faces, man.”

Suddenly, Myla sat up in bed, and her voice hardened, the laughter vanishing. “I will no longer let you shut me out again. I’ve tried to respect your boundaries, tried to understand how you felt after the surgeries, but I’m your wife, and damn it, I expect you to treat me that way. Not like someone you’ve lost feelings for but are just tolerating.”

Jared and Beck exchanged wary looks and quickly backed toward the door. Beck paused, mouthed 'whoop his ass, girl', before closing the door behind him.

“Myla! That’s not true! My God, how can you think such a thing? I love you,” Hayden protested.

“How can I think such a thing? What about the last two years you’ve been out of the hospital, Hayden? I know we couldn’t have sex, but you could've held my hand, kissed me once in a while, or just put your arm around me occasionally. Whenever I asked you how you were doing with your physical therapy, you shut me down and changed the subject. You even buried yourself in your study at mealtimes. Ninety-five percent of my meals were eaten alone or with your bestfriends! If not for them who gave me their warmth and showed their care in a hundred different ways, I wo...." She paused when her voice cracked and took a deep breath. "You fucking abandoned me, Hay.”

“It was to protect you," Hayden replied softly. "I was only half a man. I didn’t know whether I’d ever walk again or if I’d be able to make love to you like a normal man. I didn’t want you to have to deal with the pain-ridden mess I’d become, or the rage and frustration that would overcome me at the knowledge of the things I couldn’t do anymore. Christ, for almost three months I couldn’t even go to the bathroom by myself.”

“Protect me, my ass,” she snarled at him, fueled by the drugs in her. “Half a man? Give me a break. Even wheelchair-bound, you’re more man than any five thousand men off the street.

“And please, tell me I did not actually hear you say you were afraid you’d be unable to make love to me like a ‘normal man.’ Since when did you have this sudden urge to make love like a normal man? I seem to remember the conference room, and the pantry, and three other rooms in this very house that certainly do not qualify as normal. Come on, Hayden, define your concept of ‘normal’ for me.” She shouted into Hayden’s stunned face.

“And, as your wife, it’s my right to deal with your rage and frustrations and to even wipe your ass, if required. Don’t hand me any more garbage, Hayden. I’m giving you fair warning,  I will leave you if you continue like this.” Myla swiped at the tears running down her face until Hayden handed her a tissue and pulled her into his arms as best as he could.

"And I will make sure I wipe you clean in the divorce," she mumbled into his chest.

He held her tightly, his eyes misty. “I'm so sorry that I did that to you, to us. But it was such a fearful time for me. There were many times I wished that I had died in that car crash."

He pressed a kiss to her forehead. “I was wrong to handle things the way I did. I was wallowing in fear and despair and didn’t want you, or anyone else, to try to pull me out of it. I was so caught up in my self-hate and pity that I didn't think about how it was affecting you. Actually, deep down I was hoping you would leave me alone and not have to see what I'd become. I won’t try to push you aside this time, I promise.

“On another note, I would prefer to have a bidet installed rather than have you wipe my ass, if you don’t mind,” he said with a grin.

She shook her head with a watery chuckle. “You won’t get an argument out of me on that one.”

She finally managed to catch her breath and wiped her eyes with a tissue. Just as she was dropping the tissue, Jared and Beck came back into the room.

What she said before she unraveled slammed back, and her face reddened with embarrassment.

“Sorry about earlier, the ridiculous things Scott said yesterday have been echoing in my brain through the night, and whatever drug they gave me loosened my tongue." Myla looked from face to face with all the fake innocence she could muster. "So, have you boys come to take me home?”

The suspicious look Hayden gave her made her think maybe her acting wasn't all that good.

“Uh, Dr. Sorensen said I could leave. You’ve come to take me, right?”

Damn, that didn’t come out quite right.

She cleared her throat. “Home. I mean, you’ve come to take me home, right?”

Myla could feel her face heating up as they stared silently at her like there was something strange on her face.

Oh, for God's sake, why did every word out of her mouth suddenly seem to have a double meaning?

“Okay, never mind. Just leave, I’ll get dressed and call a cab... I have put my foot in my mouth enough this morning. Go on, out!” she shouted, covering her head with the bed cover.

They left silently, but their faces had an odd, pinched tightness that puzzled her. She rang for a nurse to help her dress.

It was a few minutes before one appeared, and she was laughing as she came into Myla’s room. “What on earth did you say to those three men?” the nurse asked with a grin.

“Why? What do you mean?”

The nurse helped Myla to the window and opened it as far as it would go. Myla could hear the sounds of masculine laughter. She looked out onto the park-like setting in the front of the hospital.

There, the three men were holding their sides and roaring with laughter. Hayden let out a belly laughter that nearly tipped his wheelchair over. Jared caught the chair before it could fall, and they erupted into fresh bouts of laughter.

Myla shrugged, she had no idea what she had said that was so funny, but she was very happy to see them so lighthearted. Ever since Hayden’s accident, they had all seemed so sober, so filled with responsibilities and problems. It was a sight to behold, one she wanted to see again and again.

With the nurse’s help, Myla dressed in the clothes Hayden had brought. The nurse insisted that Myla get into the wheelchair to be wheeled to the hospital doors because she’d taken a strong painkiller earlier and would probably be very dizzy and light-headed soon.

Myla reluctantly agreed, but she did get a kick out of it when Hayden maneuvered his big motorized wheelchair beside her smaller, dainty one as the nurse pushed her down the hallway.

Outside the hospital doors, Beck carefully scooped Myla out of her wheelchair, and before he could turn around, Myla looked at Hayden’s wheelchair and the wheelchair she’d just left.

“She’s going to miss you.” She mumbled. “I’m okay, musketeers. Is it one for all, or is it all for one? I can’t remember...”

“What on earth are you talking about, Myla?” Hayden’s brow wrinkled in concern.

“My delicate little push mobile really liked your big, beautiful electric monster there.”

Jared chuckled.

Hayden smiled faintly. "The medication they gave you must be the premium one."

“Will you hold my hand?” she asked him uncertainly.

“Baby, of course, I’ll hold your hand. You're everything to me, Mine. Always remember that.”

Myla took in a breath as she felt her eyes sting with tears. It has been a long since he called her 'Mine'. Maybe this would get better from now on.

The Day I Died And Reborn
VALERIANA

The day I died was the day my husband married my step sister. 

I was lying on a thin, moldy mattress in the dark dampness of the basement, my fingers clawing at the sheets as another wave of pain vibrated through the veins of my body. And even in such pain, I could hear the loud howling of the Silver Moon pack.

"Celebrate today!" The announcer's voice echoed, ringing into my ears. "Our Alpha, Silas, and his true Luna, Elara, are finally wed! Fifteen years of love, united at last!"

My mate, Silas, the man I had given my Alpha birthright to, the man for whom I had traded my pride, my strength, and eventually, my freedom; was getting married to my stepsister.

My heart shattered in pieces. I tried to shut my ears from listening to the happiness that was supposed to be mine. But the more I tried, the louder it became.

"Push, you useless bitch," a servant snapped, shoving a rag into my mouth. "Hurry up and drop the pup. Your only purpose left is to bear an heir for the Alpha. Heirs from fated mates are exceptionally strong. So stop your whining and push!"

I bit down on the rag, shutting my eyes while I let the hot tears fall down my cheeks. The searing pain nearly made me black out. I bit down hard on my tongue to stay conscious, for I couldn’t give up now.

I wanted to see my baby!

And my father was still waiting for me to save him!

Silas had promised to spare his life if I gave him an heir. So I pushed, even though it felt like every single being in me was tearing apart.

"Ahhh!" I cried, grabbing the sheets even tighter.

The door of the basement banged open, letting the ray of light from the hallway slip in. Elara walked in gracefully, like a bride stepping into a ballroom. Her hand flew to her nose, pretending to be bothered by the smell.

Staring down at my pale trembling legs, she shook her head. “How pitiful,” she said, clicking her tongue.

“What do you want from me, Elara?” I asked in between gasps.

“Want?” She scoffed. “That's an understatement, Val. Do you really think I would let a wretched thing like you bear his heir? My position as Silas's rightful Luna is now sealed. That thing in your womb had already been dead for three days. I made sure the tonic I gave you worked slowly.”

My eyes flew open in disbelief as I stared at the very person I used to call a sister. 

“You killed…” I stuttered, tears streaming heavily down my eyes. “You killed my baby?”

“Yes?” She shrugged in a nonchalant way.

“No!” I shook my head. “No, this can’t be real!”

"Oh yes," she continued. "And as for your father?" She leaned down, her lips twisting into a venomous smile. "He will be executed soon. Silas already signed the order himself this morning. He said he was tired of cleaning up your family's mess."

"No. You're lying," I shrieked, clawing at the air. "That's not true."

"Of course, it is.” She pulled away. “Who asked you to meddle in our precious chosen mate relationship?" She sneered. "Now you face the consequences."

“Why?” I croaked. “Why do you hate— AHH!” A sharp pain exploded my abdomen, forcing the baby out of my vagina. My head fell to the side, my breathing coming out in short gasps as I stared at Elara with weak eyes.

“My baby,” I whispered. “I want to see my baby.”

The servant brought the lifeless being to my me, dropping him to my side. I touched his face with shaky hands, like he was alive.

With the last of my strength, I mind-link to Silas. "Silas, please! Save my father! I'll go away. I'll never love you again, I promise. Just save him!"

I hated myself. I should never have chased him. I should never have believed that being fated mates meant he would love me. I should never have given up my Alpha position to a man who saw me as nothing but scrap.

If I had stayed strong, if I had protected my father, would everything be different?

The door banged open again, Silas stepped in. He still had his wedding suit on, looking regal and terrifyingly handsome. His eyes fell on me.

"Is it done?" he asked coldly.

"It's a stillborn, Silas," Elara said, her voice suddenly turning so fragile. "She couldn't even do this one thing right."

Silas glared at the tiny blue-tinged body on the edge of the bed. His face twisted into a deep frown, his lip curling in disgust. "Throw it in the woods!”

"Silas," I croaked, reaching out a trembling, bloody hand towards him.

"Don't touch me you filthy bitch!" He cursed, taking a few steps back, as if my touch would stain him. "Is there anything you can do right in this life of yours?"

I looked at him, really looked at him. "Silas… it's me."

"And so?" He snapped, his brows furrowing. "Does that change anything? Does that make things better? Even to bear a child is a curse to you."

I shook my head slightly, wishing all these were an act of my imagination. Yet, reality kept proving itself to me. 

"Did you ever love me? Even for a second? Did you ever cherish me?”

“Wasn't it obvious?” He frowned. “I never loved you, Valeriana, not even a bit. Who in his right mind would want to love someone like you?” 

Those words tore whatever that was left holding my heart. “I thought we were fated mates!"

“Fated?” He scoffed, chuckling. “The Moon Goddess played a joke on me, tying me to a weak, pathetic girl like you. I felt disgusted every time I had to touch you, Valeriana. I only tolerated you for the power your father gave me. Now that I have it, you are useless now.”

He turned to Elara, his expression softening into something I had craved for years. “Come, my love. The guests are waiting. We shouldn't keep the pack waiting for our first dance.”

“Silas!” I called out, stretching my arm like they would reach him. “Please...” 

The door slammed shut.

I stared at my baby, letting the tears fall even more. I'm sorry, Father, I really am. I am sorry for being a fool, for letting love ruin everything we had. 

If I could go back, if I could have one more chance, I swear I would never love him again. I would burn this world before I let him touch me.

The servant screamed. “Oh my goodness! She's bleeding!” 

They rushed, doing everything in their power to stop the bleeding, but it didn't. And every second, I felt life slipping away. Still looking at my child, I whispered. “I'm sorry I wasn't a good mother.”

My eyes began to close, darkness slowly wrapping its arms around me. I thought I had a voice in my mind, but I couldn't make out the words.

And then everything went black.

****
An ancient voice sighed in the darkness of my mind. "Wake up, little wolf." 

I jolted my eyes open, sucking in heavy air. 

A familiar desk came into sight. On it lay my favorite romance novel from my school days, and there seemed to be some words carved underneath the book. Sunlight streamed in through the window on the right, falling gently on my hands.

I froze, my eyes widened.

I stared down at my hands, they should have been as rough from years of scrubbing floors in the basement of the park house. But now they were soft, my nails perfectly trimmed, and my skin glowed with health of youth.

I looked just like the eighteen-year-old daughter of an Alpha I once was.

I reached for the desktop in a rush, I grabbed the small makeup mirror on my desk before me. My hands flew to my face, feeling the soft texture of my skin. 

The face in the mirror sent a jolt through my entire body.

Pink cheeks, eyes untouched by suffering, and a fresh scar on my forehead—the one I’d gotten from a fall at eighteen, a scar that had stayed with me for ten long years. Right now, it was still bright red and newly healed, not fully faded yet.

This was me at eighteen!

I’d been reborn back to my eighteen-year-old self!

All sounds crashed back like a tidal wave. Footsteps, chatter, the scraping creak of dragged chairs. People laughed and bickered, everything vivid and almost surreal.

Before I could recover from my shock, a shadow loomed over me.

“Valeriana!”

His voice vibrated through the walls of the room, his face twisted in anger as he stormed towards me. In a force, he slammed his fist on my desk, the sound causing every head to turn in our direction.

"Why are you here?" He growled, his eyes flashing with annoyance. “I told you ten minutes ago to go to the cafe across the street. Elara wants a sugar-free peach tea and those imported macarons. Why haven't you left yet?”

No Longer His Fool
VALERIANA

A strange sense of vertigo rushed through me as I stared at Silas from head to toe. 

He was undeniably handsome, no doubt. Sharp jawline, dark hair that fell just right, those intense gray eyes that used to make my stomach flip. And he had that easy, arrogant smile that suggested the world belonged to him.

If I had truly been eighteen again, if I didn't remember the basement, and how he had signed to execute my father, I would have been staring at him right now with a red face and a pounding heart.

Because l liked him for years.

Even before we entered this academy, I followed him around like a fool. Laughed at his silly jokes, and made sure his favourite snacks were always in his locker. When we found out we were fated mates at nineteen, I cried my eyes out from happiness. I thought the Moon Goddess had finally rewarded my loyalty. I thought all those years of chasing him had finally meant something.

I was so blinded by destiny that I gave up my position as an Alpha daughter just so he could feel like my equal. But looking at him now, I didn't see a hero. I saw a thief.

"Are you still sitting there?" Silas snapped, his brows furrowing. "Valeriana, I’m talking to you. The cafe closes its morning shift in ten minutes. Go."

The students around us were already whispering. I could hear their muffled giggles and crazy comments.

“There she goes again,” a girl behind me muttered. “Running errands like his personal assistant.”

“She has no pride at all,” someone else said. “If a guy treated me like that, I’d disappear.”

Another voice added, “Silas doesn’t even look at her properly. Why does she keep chasing him?”

“She’s been following him for years. Jeez, it’s embarrassing.”

“I heard he only cares about Elara.”

“Obviously. Can’t you see how gentle he is with Elara? With her, he’s always cold.”

In my previous life, those words would have torn my heart apart. I would pretend not to hear them, but I would go back to my room and cry into my pillow. Then the next day, I would chase him again as if nothing had happened.

I thought love meant endurance then. I thought if I stayed long enough, tried hard enough, he would eventually turn around and see me. Yet all I’d gotten in return was endless pain and betrayal.

Now, listening to them again, I would never be that tearful girl anymore. I knew I was going to change everything.

"I heard you the first time, Silas," I said, nonchalantly. "I just don't care."

Silas blinked, his mouth hanging open slightly. "What?"

"I'm not going," I insisted. I picked up my bag, slinging it over my shoulder. "If you want to play waiter for Elara, do it yourself. I have my own things to take care of."

"Is this a joke?" Silas stepped closer, his face reddening. He was used to my absolute devotion. "Are you throwing a tantrum because I walked Elara to class this morning? Grow up, Valeriana. You’re being petty."

"Call it whatever you want," I said, stepping around him. "Just move out of my way."

I walked past him without a second glance. The silence in the room was so deafening you could hear the hum of the overhead lights. Silas didn't follow me, his pride wouldn't let him. But I could feel his burning gaze on my back.

I pushed open the doors of the classroom and stepped out. The morning air beat against my skin, filling my lungs with the scent of pine. I closed my eyes, tilting my head to the sun, My heart leaped with pure joy.

It was real. I was truly reborn!

I wasn't that broken, bleeding woman in the basement anymore. I was young, healthy, and I was powerful. 

Thank you, Cynthia, I whispered in my mind. I won't waste this chance.

I walked down the hallway, glancing around the school I knew all too well.

Blackwood Academy was jointly founded by five major packs to foster peace, which meant everyone wore the same uniform and ranks were supposed to be hidden. 

But wolves are creatures with an innate strict hierarchy mindset by nature. Everyone spent their days trying to figure out who the future Alphas were. And then they'd make their assumptions and curry favor with whoever they thought mattered.

Clearly, not all of their guesses were right. Especially when it came to Elara and me—

I saw her as I walked down the main hallway toward the library. 

Elara was sitting on a velvet bench, surrounded by a group of girls who hung on her every word. 

Everyone thought Elara was of noble blood. She was smart, she carried herself like a porcelain doll, and she always had the newest designer bags and jewelry. But what they didn't know is; those luxury items were bought by Silas with my money.

I wanted to walk past them, to ignore the trash and start planning my next move, but Elara had always been an expert at spotting a change in the wind.

"Valeriana?" she called out.

The group of girls turned. Elara stood up, looking at me with wide, concerned eyes. She appeared so innocent, so fragile. The same act she had used to ruin my life.

"Valeriana, I’m so sorry," she said, hurrying over to me. She reached out to grab my hand, but I pulled back before she could touch me. She faltered, her expression flickering with confusion. "Silas told me he asked you to get those macarons... I told him not to! Please don't be mad at him."

"I'm not mad at him, Elara," I said, looking her dead in the eye. "I just realized that I'm not a courier service. If you want expensive sweets, buy them yourself."

Elara’s lip trembled. She was a master of the victim look. "I... I just thought…” Then she looked down. “I didn't mean to upset you."

One of the girls behind her, maybe named Sophie, stepped forward. "Wow, Valeriana. Why are you being such a bitch? Elara is just being nice. It’s not her fault Silas likes helping her more than he likes helping you."

Elara suddenly pressed a hand to her chest and began to cough. It was a soft, hacking sound—the kind of cough that made men want to wrap her in a blanket and carry her.

"Oh no, Elara! Are you okay?" the girls crowded around her.

"I'm fine," Elara wheezed, her eyes watering. "I just don't want to cause trouble between Valeriana and Silas."

"You're not causing trouble," a loud, angry voice boomed from the end of the hall.

I didn’t even need to turn around to know who it was.. Silas.

He was marching toward us, his face wearing a mask of fury. In his hand, he held a white paper bag from the cafe—the macarons. He must have run there and back for his loved Elara.

He shoved his way through the group and grabbed Elara by the shoulders. "Elara! Are you okay? I heard you coughing from the stairs."

"I'm okay, Silas," she whispered, leaning her head against his chest. "Valeriana was just... she was just explaining that she won't help me anymore. I understand. She doesn't like me, after all."

Silas’s head whipped around to look at me. If looks could kill, I’d be buried in the school garden.

"What… did you do to her?"

Never. Again.
VALERIANA
 
Watching Silas hover over Elara, tucking a stray hair behind her ear with that look of panicked devotion, made my stomach turn. It was a sickening sense of déjà vu, felt exactly like watching them together while I lay dying in that basement.

They had been this intimate, this bold, right under my nose for years, and I had been too blinded by fate to see it until my final breath.

The memory of my poor baby flashed in my mind, turning my grief into a heated rage.

I looked at Elara, who was currently leaning into Silas as if she might shatter at any moment. 

"You really should win an award, Elara," I said, my voice dripping with sarcasm. "The coughing, the trembling, the watery eyes. It’s a masterpiece. Have you considered a career in theater? You’re clearly wasted here at the Academy."

Silas’s face contorted. He opened his mouth to bark at me, but Elara reached up and caught his sleeve with a delicate, shaking hand.

"No, Silas, please," she whispered, but loud enough for the growing crowd of students to hear. "Don’t be angry with Valeriana. She’s just... in a terrible mood right now. She didn't mean to be so cruel. I'm sure she’s just tired."

Then she looked at me, her eyes wide and brimming with fake tears. "I forgive you, Valeriana. I know you didn't mean those mean things."

I scoffed at how she was playing the saintly victim while making me look like a mental case.

But Silas fell for it instantly. He looked at her with such pride before turning that gaze on me, transformed into pure disgust."Do you see this, Valeriana?" Silas snarled. "Elara is half-fainting, yet she’s still defending you. She has more grace in her pinky finger than you have in your entire body."

He stepped closer, a smug, knowing look crossing his face."I get it now. This is all a show, isn't it? You’re acting rebellious because I’ve been paying you no mind lately. You’re trying to get my attention by being difficult. Let me tell you something! This cheap trick is disgusting! You’ve been disobedient and loud, and it only makes me loathe you more!"

I stared at him, genuinely stunned for a second. The audacity of his words was almost impressive.Disobedient? he called me disobedient?

I thought back to the girl I used to be.

I remembered skipping my own father's birthday dinner because he had an "emergency", which turned out to be him needing company while he picked out a gift for Elara.

I remembered standing in the rain for three hours because he'd said he wanted to talk, and he never showed up, never even texted, and I just waited like an idiot thinking maybe he'd still come.

I remembered giving up my wealthy position for him. My birthright. My entire future. Because he'd convinced me that's what a good mate did—supported her husband, stood behind him instead of beside him.

I had spent years bowing, scraping, and dimming my own light just to make sure his ego stayed inflated.

The sheer absurdity of him calling me disobedient was too much, and I couldn’t help but let out a cold laugh.

"What’s so funny?" Silas demanded, his face darkening.

"You are," I said, wiping a mock tear from my eye. "You really think I’m doing this for you? Silas, look at yourself. You’re not even worth the effort of a trick. So, don't try to feel too big with your crazy assumptions."

"Valeriana!" Silas roared. "Know your place! Don't you dare speak to me like that. You’ll regret this. You’ll come crawling back to me, crying and begging for my forgiveness like you always do. And I’m telling you now, I won't make it easy for you."

I smiled in satisfaction, seeing the angry expression on his face. "The person who’s going to be begging on their knees won't be me, Silas. Keep that in mind."

By now, a large crowd had gathered. Students were leaning over the balcony, watching the drama unfold. Elara saw the audience and seemed to decide to turn up the heat. She stepped forward, dabbing her eyes with a silk handkerchief.

"Valeriana, please," she sobbed. "Why are you being so loud? Everyone is watching, aren’t you the least bit embarrassed? If you’re jealous of me and Silas, we can talk about it privately. You don't have to make such a scene and hurt Silas’s reputation."

I turned to her, my expression going stone-cold."His reputation? What reputation could he possibly have? And as for being embarrassing, the only shameful thing here is a girl who puts on an innocent act and sheds fake tears."

"How can you say that?" A girl in the crowd shouted. "Elara is a high-rank wolf! Look at how she carries herself. She’s way more noble than you."

"Yeah," another student chimed in, whispering loudly. "Silas and Elara look like true Alpha's heirs. They have the grades, the looks... Silas must be the son of some powerful Alpha from the North. He’s way too impressive to be just anyone."

I looked at Silas. He was standing there, soaking in the compliments. He didn't say a word to correct them. In fact, he loved that they thought he was royalty.

But the truth was, even if Silas desperately wanted to bury it. 

He wasn't the son of an Alpha.

He was the son of my father’s bodyguard. He had been living under my family’s roof, eating our food, and wearing the clothes we provided for years. And yet, there he stood, preening in front of everyone as if he owned the world.

In my past life, I had helped him hide it. I didn't want him to feel embarrassed. I had protected his ego at the cost of my own pride.

I lowered my head, gathering my thoughts. Silas must have mistook my silence for weakness. He thought he had finally backed me into a corner.

He stepped forward, trying to reclaim his dominance in front of the witnesses.

"Look at you," Silas said, shaking his head with mock pity. "You know you’ve gone too far. Now, I’m going to be generous. If you apologize to Elara right now—on your knees—and admit your wrongs, I’ll forgive you. I’ll let you walk away and we can pretend this didn't happen. It’s your last chance, Valeriana. Don't waste it."

Elara looked at me, a tiny, smug glint in her eyes. She was waiting for me to apologize. And I could tell the students were waiting for someone like me, a low-rank nobody, to bow down to the so-called noble Silas and Elara.

I took a deep breath. I looked Silas directly in the eye, seeing every bit of his arrogance.

"I have two words for you, Silas," I said, my voice echoing every corner of the hallway.

"I’m waiting," Silas smirked.

"Never. Again."

The smirk slid off his face.

"I will never apologize to her," I declared, stepping closer until I was inches from his chest. "And I will never, ever be the girl you can order around again. If she wants an apology, then she should go find a mirror and apologize to herself for being such a disappointment."

Silas froze, his mouth hanging open. He looked as if I had reached out and slapped him across the face.

I Will Never Love You
SILAS
 
I stood in the middle of the hallway, my heart thudding against my ribs so fast I stared right into those now angry eyes.

What the hell just happened?

This wasn't Valeriana. 

The Valeriana I knew was soft. She was the girl who, just last month, spent four hours standing outside the gym because I told her I’d forgotten my lucky headband. When I finally came out, she was shivering, but she had smiled and handed it to me as if I’d done her a favor by letting her wait.

She was the girl who, during the pack’s last hunting ceremony, had purposely tripped during the final sprint so I could take the kill and look like the stronger hunter in front of the elders. She lived to make me look good.

There was no way she could change this fast. It had to be an act. 

She was probably reading some "how to catch a man" book or listening to someone’s advice on how to be "mysterious."

"Did she really just say that?" a guy from the back of the crowd laughed. "An Omega maid trying to play hard to get with the Alpha’s son? That’s bold."

"She’s definitely desperate," a girl added, sneering. "She knows Silas has always had eyes for Elara, so she’s throwing a tantrum to make him chase her. It’s pathetic to force an Alpha's son to do what he doesn't want."

The words settled into my brain, and I felt a wave of relief wash over me. 

Of course. That was it. She wasn't angry. She was terrified. She was terrified that I was finally choosing Elara over her. She loved me too much, so she acted out like a wounded animal to get my attention.

I adjusted my jacket, regaining my composure. A small, arrogant smirk pulled at my lips. Nice try, Val, but you're not that good an actress.

But she chuckled, like everything was funny rather than hurting. 

"Alpha's son?" She asked, looking at the watching crowd, then back at me. "Is that what you told them, Silas? Or did you just let them assume?"

My blood ran cold, the smirk on my face vanished instantly.

I felt a bead of sweat prickle at my hairline. I wasn't an Alpha’s son. My father had been the head of the Alpha’s guard—a brave man, yes, but a servant nonetheless. When my mother died years ago, Alpha Marcus had taken me into the main house as a ward, giving me a room and a life that didn't belong to me.

At first, when the rumors started at school that I was the Alpha's secret heir, I hated it. I didn't want people to think I only had talent because of some blood. I wanted to be an elite through my own hard work. 

However, as the assumption grew, people gave me the best seats. They did my chores. They respect me and treat me like I mattered, and I told myself it was fine, that I'd prove myself owe it through my own merit anyway. 

But Valeriana knew. She knew exactly where I came from.

Before I could find my voice, Elara stepped in. She gracefully slid her arm through mine, leaning her head on my shoulder.

"Valeriana, please don't start talking about ranks and bloodlines," Elara said softly, looking at the crowd with a saintly expression. "We’re at school. The founders said everyone is equal here."

"She’s right!" someone shouted. "Elara is so humble, even though she's clearly high-born. Valeriana is just obsessed with status because she has nothing else."

I looked down at Elara. She was so kind, so gentle. Unlike Valeriana, who was now using my past as a weapon.

"Elara is right," I said, my voice gaining strength as I looked at Valeriana with narrowed eyes. "Don't break school rules by discussing rank improperly, Valeriana."

I pulled Elara closer, tucking her under my arm to show everyone where my loyalty lay. 

"And don't waste your breath with these little games," I added, pitching my voice so the whole hall could hear. "You can act as tough as you want, but it won't change the truth. I will never love you, Valeriana. You’re just not the one for me."

****
VALERIANA
 
"I will never love you, Valeriana."

I stared at Silas, and for a second, I almost laughed again. In my past life, those words would have been a death sentence. I would have crumbled to the floor, sobbing and promising to change.

But now? All I saw was a boy standing on a pedestal I had built for him, telling me he wouldn't let me sit at his feet.

How could I have been so blind? I wondered. He was so self-absorbed, so convinced that the world revolved around his ego. He actually thought I was doing all of this for a chance to be with him. 

He didn't know, after the basement, after my poor baby, after the execution of my father, the idea of loving him was like the idea of loving a plague.

I looked directly into his eyes, letting all the heat and anger fade into a cold, dead indifference.

"That you’ll never love me?" I said. "Even better. I was starting to worry I’d have to find a way to get rid of you myself."

The crowd’s laughter died down. They looked confused.  

I didn't give them another second of my time. I turned my back on Silas and Elara, walking away with a lightness in my step that I hadn't felt in years.

I made it to the end of the hallway and ducked into a quiet stairwell. My heart was racing. I had actually done it. I had stood up to him.

Suddenly, the phone in my pocket vibrated. I pulled it out and saw the caller ID. Dad.

Quickly, I pressed the answer button. "H-hello?"

"Valeriana? Sweetheart, is that you?" The voice was deep, and full of the strength I remembered from my childhood. It was my father. He was alive. He was okay.

Tears blurred my vision instantly. I leaned against the cold brick wall, my chest aching. "Dad..."

"Val? What’s wrong? You sound... are you crying?" A hint of concern stained in his voice. I could hear him shifting papers on his desk. "Is it Silas again? Did Silas say something to upset you? I swear, if he’s being ungrateful after everything we’ve done for him..."

"No, Dad," I interrupted, wiping my eyes with the back of my hand. "It’s not like that. I'm crying because... I don't love him anymore. I'm done with Silas. Truly done."

There was a long silence on the other end of the line. Then, I heard a heavy sigh, followed by a low, triumphant chuckle. 

"Finally," my father breathed. "To be honest, Val, maybe he’s a good student, but he’s not the man for my daughter. You’re an Alpha’s daughter, Valeriana. You need someone who stands beside you, not someone you have to carry."

"I know, Dad," I whispered. "I see that now."

"I'm proud of you, sweetheart. Truly. It takes a lot of strength to admit when you've been chasing the wrong star." He paused, and I could practically hear the gears turning in his head. "Since you've cleared some space in your heart... how about I help you fill it? How about I arrange a proper fiancé for you?"

Every being in me went still. "What?”

Fiancé?
VALERIANA
 
A fiancé?

My mind flashed back to my past life. I did have a fiancé once. Or rather, a man my father had tried to make me accept before I begged and pleaded to be with Silas.

His name was Alejandro Thorne, the Alpha of the Shadow Ridge Pack. Alejandro was known as the Black Wolf, a man as cold as ice and just as deadly.

His pack and mine were the two most powerful packs in the realm, locked in constant rivalry across every field of influence. We had hated each other since we were children. Every time we met to settle disputed matters, we spent the entire time trying to out-snarl each other. The idea of being his wife felt like a joke. Him and me? It was impossible. He would sooner rip my throat out than hold my hand.

I opened my mouth to protest, to tell my father that I would rather be a rogue than marry a Thorne, but the shrill, piercing scream of the school bell drowned out my voice.

Dad's voice crackled through in pieces: "...when you get home..." "...discuss properly..."

"Dad? I can't hear you!" I shouted over the noise of hundreds of lockers slamming and students flooding the halls.

I looked at the date on my phone screen. Friday. The mid-semester break started tomorrow. We would all be sent home to our respective packs for a week.

"I have to go, Dad! I’ll be home by afternoon. We’ll talk then!"

I hung up before he could say more. 

A fiancé. My father wanted to arrange that engagement with Alejandro Thorne again. My heart was pounding against my ribs. No, I would never agree with this! I'd have to deal with this fiancé situation as soon as possible.

I turned the corner toward my locker, my head faced down as I tried to wipe the stray tears from my face. I didn't want anyone to see me like this. But as I reached my row, I walked straight into a wall of solid chest and familiar laundry detergent.

I stumbled back, barely raising my face to look.

"Going somewhere in a hurry?"

I finally looked up. Silas was standing there with his arms crossed, watching me with a look of intense curiosity. Elara was right beside him, her hand tucked into the crook of his elbow like she was marking her territory.

Silas’s eyes raked over my face, lingering on my red eyes. He raised an eyebrow, a flicker of satisfaction crossing his features. 

"Oh, Valeriana, you've been crying?" Silas teased, a small, mocking smile playing on his lips. "What happened to that big talk from earlier? 'Never. Again,' wasn't it? And here you are, hiding in the stairwell and crying your eyes out. 

I didn't say a word, I just reached for my locker handle.

"You really shouldn't try so hard to be something you're not," Silas continued, leaning against the locker next to mine. "You're soft, Val. You always have been. You put on a show to try and make me jealous, but the second you're alone, you break down. It’s okay. Only I would put up with these moods of yours. Just apologize to Elara, and I might consider letting you come back with me."

I ignored him yet again. I pulled my locker open and began shoving my textbooks into my bag. I could feel his gaze burning into the side of my head.

Elara was watching Silas, and for a split second, I saw a shadow flash across her eyes. She didn't like the way he was looking at me, even if it was with mockery, he was looking. She quickly tightened her grip on his arm and pulled him toward his own locker, which was just a few feet away.

"Come on, Silas," Elara said, her voice dripping with artificial sweetness. "Let me help you pack. You know how you always forget your charger."

She started fussing over his bag, acting the part of the perfect, doting partner. She was talking in a low voice, but she made sure her words were loud enough for me to hear.

"Don't be too hard on her, Silas," Elara whispered. "She’s just being stubborn, in a foul mood and throwing a petty fit. She’ll return to normal soon enough once she realizes."

I saw Silas’s face darken slightly. He didn't look at her, he was staring at the floor. Elara noticed his distraction and her movements became more frantic. She reached deep into the back of his locker, pulling out a small, dusty box.

"Oh! What's this?" she asked, surprised.

She opened the box and pulled out a hand-carved wooden wolf. It was small, with a blue ribbon tied around its neck.

I froze. 

I knew that wolf. I had spent three weeks carving it by hand when I was fourteen. It was the first gift I ever gave Silas. I had cut my fingers a dozen times on the wood, wanting it to be perfect. I had given it to himon the anniversary of his mother’s passing, telling him that as long as he had this, he would never be alone. 

I had assumed he’d thrown it away years ago. I thought it was buried in some landfill, or down in the deepest part of ground. But he had it. 

"Valeriana give this to you?" Elara asked, her eyes narrowing as she looked at the toy. She looked at Silas. "You still kept it? All this time? Silas... you don't mean to tell me you actually care about this piece of wood?"

Elara’s words made me pause. Could Silas actually care about a gift I’d given him? It sounded more absurd than anything. My eyes clung to that wooden wolf, the object that held all the love I’d wasted on him, all the devotion I’d poured into someone who never deserved it.

Silas looked at the wolf in her hand. For a heartbeat, his expression seemed to soften. His fingers reached out as if to touch the wood.

But then he looked at me. He saw me watching the wooden wolf, His face turned to stone. He snatched the wooden wolf out of Elara’s hand.

"It’s just trash," he said, his voice cold and loud. "I forgot it was even in there. I’ve been too lazy to clean out the junk at the back."

Before I could blink, he turned and threw the wolf into the metal trash can at the end of the row. It hit the bottom with a thud.

Silas looked at me straight in the eye with a cruel gaze. "Some things are just too much effort to dispose of until they start taking up too much space."

I knew he was talking about me. He might as well have said it out loud—that I was just forgotten trash he couldn’t be bothered to deal with anymore.

When I didn’t react, his face twisted into a deep frown, his lip curling in disgust. It was the exact same look he’d worn when he’d ordered them to get rid of my baby.

"The same goes for people. Anyone useless should be thrown away like a corpse!”

So he thrown our dead child.

My heart sank completely.

Who the Hell is He?
SILAS 
 
The sound of that wooden wolf hitting the bottom of the trash can was louder than I expected. For a second, as I watched Valeriana’s face go pale, my chest tightened inexplicably. 

I almost reached back into the bin to pull it out. The thought slammed into me before I could stop it.

I remembered when she gave it to me. I remembered the bandages on her fingers from the carving tools and the way her eyes had searched mine, desperate to comfort me when I was drowning in grief on my mother’s death anniversary. She had been so kind back then. So... real.

“Silas, are you OK?"

Elara’s soft, concerned voice cut through my thoughts, her fingers gently tugging at the hem of my shirt. That meek, docile look of hers dragged my mind back to what happened years ago.

That day, I found Elara sobbing in the garden, she told me through gasps how Valeriana had humiliated her and reminded her that she was nothing but an Omega servant. 

That was the day the scales fell from my eyes. 

I realized Valeriana wasn't kind. All her kindness had just been an act, a mask hiding what she really was underneath. She was just a spoiled, privileged girl who used her status to crush anyone she deemed lesser.

After that, I'd hated her.

I hated that side of her. So no. I didn't regret throwing away that worthless piece of wood. I didn't.

Fuck that. What did I have to regret? It was garbage. Nothing but charity from a spoiled elite.

'It’s just trash,' I told myself, hardening my heart until it felt like a cold stone. 'She’s just getting what she deserves. It’s time she learned that her money can't buy my respect.'

I forced down the strange feeling in my chest, my gaze involuntarily meeting Valeriana. 

She didn't throw a tantrum like the brat I told myself she was. She just packed her bag quickly and headed towards the exit without looking back. There was something I couldn't read in her silence.

"Come on, Silas," Elara whispered, squeezing my hand. "Let’s get to the gate. I heard some of the seniors brought their family's sports cars today. It’s going to be a madhouse."

Truth be told, I’d already grabbed my bag the second she finished speaking, my feet moving toward the entrance on instinct. My strides were long, forcing Elara to hurry and trot just to keep up beside me.

I walked forward, shoving my hands into my pockets and trying to shake off the image of that wooden wolf thrown right in the trash can.

The school gates were packed with a massive crowd. This was the one day each year when Blackwood Academy’s fake equality crumbled completely. Everyone craned to spot arriving parents and luxury vehicles, quick to label each student by their family wealth and pack standing.

It was a game of status, and I usually won it.

Usually, Valeriana’s driver arrived in a black luxury sedan—the kind of car that screamed old money and power. Since Valeriana was so obsessed with me, she always made sure the driver picked me up first or dropped me off at the gate in style. She hated for me to lose face.

The moment I stepped onto the sidewalk, a group of guys from the football team surrounded us. These were guys who usually spent their time acting tough and big, but now they were looking at me with grins that were a little too wide.

"Hey, Silas! Bet your ride is going to be the best one here, right?" one of them laughed, clapping me on the shoulder. "The Alpha’s son can't be seen in a minivan."

"I heard his family has a fleet of Italian imports," a girl whispered loudly to her friend, looking at me with wide, admiring eyes. "He’s probably got a custom-made engine."

I didn't say anything. I just stood there with a cool, detached expression, letting them talk. 

In my head, I decided that if Valeriana had apologized for her behavior earlier, if she had come crawling back and begged for my forgiveness, I might actually let her sit next to me today. I might even forgive her a little for the trash comment. I’d let her bask in the reflected glory of everyone watching us leave.

"Look at that!" someone screamed, pointing down the road.

The familiar black luxury SUV drove toward the gates. It was the same high-end car the Alpha always sent to pick us up specially for the holidays. The crowd gasped, causing my heart to swell with pride. I loved it when they looked surprised at my entry.

"Well," I said, giving Elara a confident smile and nodding to the guys. I felt like I was ten feet tall. "See you all after the break."

I stepped away from the crowd, my chest puffed out as they kept cheering me, saying words of praise I never knew my head could contain. I felt the heat of a dozen cameras on my back as students pulled out their phones. I walked toward the black beast as it slowed to a crawl. I was already reaching for the door handle, ready to show everyone exactly who I was.

But I wasn't the first one there. 

Valeriana had appeared out of nowhere. She moved with a grace I hadn't noticed before, stepping right past me as if I were a ghost. Before I could say a word, she reached out and opened the rear door with ease, as if she had been expecting this car all along.

The crowd went dead silent, my hand freezing mid-air.

What the fuck? What the hell is she doing? My heart slammed wildly in my chest from the shock. 

"Valeriana! What are you doing!" I stepped toward her, lowering my voice just enough for her to hear clearly. "Stop making a fool of yourself!"

She didn't even turn around, already stepping forward to climb into the car.

Suddenly, a hand reached out from the darkness of the car’s interior. 

It was a man’s hand—large, with well-defined knuckles and a heavy silver ring on the index finger. He didn't just open the door further, he reached out and wrapped his fingers firmly around Valeriana’s wrist, pulling her inside.

The sight sent a jolt of pure, unadulterated rage through my veins.

"Silas?" Elara ran up behind me, touching my arm. "What’s going on?"

I didn't answer her. I shoved her hand off me and strode to the car.

I blocked the door before Valeriana could pull it shut. I leaned into the air-conditioned coolness of the car, my eyes flashing with a predatory light. I could feel my wolf was scratching at the surface, snarling at the intrusion.

But the scene unfolding before me instantly left me frozen stiff.

A man was sitting extremely close to Valeriana, so close their shoulders were touching. He was draped in a charcoal suit that looked like it cost more than my entire tuition. He had dark hair, and eyes that looked like frozen chips of ice. 

He was still holding her wrist, his thumb grazing her skin in a way that felt sickeningly intimate.

Then my gaze shifted to Valeriana. I expected to see fear. I expected her to look at me with those big, teary eyes, pleading for me to save her from this stranger. 

Instead, she looked at me with a bored, tired expression.

My wolf snapped completely out of control inside me, roaring so fiercely I felt like I might burst apart. The power coming off this stranger was suffocating, but my anger wouldn't stop burning.

"Who the hell is he?" I roared, my voice vibrating against the car's leather interior. 

"What the hell are you doing in the car?!"
0:00 / 0:38

Your warm eye mask may bring heat.

It may also bring a hard shell, a tight band, and weight on the face.

That is the trade no one puts on the box.

No, warm masks have not been shown to cause glaucoma. But studies do show that pressing an eye into a pillow can raise eye pressure for a short time.

So the question is not, "Will this mask give me glaucoma?"

The real question is, "Why press more gear against closed, sensitive eyes when there is a lighter way?"

Warm eye care should not feel like lifting weights with your face.

But look at many heated masks.

There is a hard plastic shell. A thick band. A battery. Buttons. A charger. Foam around the eyes. All of it must sit somewhere. Much of it sits on the face.

For eyes that already feel tired or sore, that bulk can be hard to ignore.

One group member said heated masks put "too much pressure" on the eyes. Another said many USB masks did not feel warm enough. That leaves a bad trade.

More gear. More weight. Yet not always the warm break people hoped for.

Novlora was made around a simpler idea.

Keep the soft part. Keep the warmth. Remove the bulky machine.

Each Lutein MicroSteam patch comes fresh-sealed. Open it when you are ready. Place it over closed eyes. The patch warms by itself, so there is no hard shell to charge and no cord to keep near the bed.

There is also no need to test a hot bean bag against your hand. No need to wonder if one microwave made it warmer than the last. No need to stop, walk back, and heat a cold cloth again.

It feels more like a soft eye patch than a device.

That makes it easy to keep close. Put a sachet by the couch. Add a few to a travel bag. Reach for one after a long day of screens, dry air, or bright light.

The scale test is simple.

One side gives you a rigid mask, tight band, and cable.

The other gives you a thin patch and a quiet break.

Novlora does not promise to cure dry eye. It does not replace drops or the plan from an eye doctor. It gives the warm step a lighter form, with less gear between you and the moment of calm.

No bulky shell. No charging cord. No thick band.

Just open, place, and unwind.

Try Novlora with a 30-day money-back promise.
